# Changelog Generation

2. List all merge commits since that tag: `git log <tag>..HEAD --merges --format='%s' | grep -v "Merge branch"`

## Where the OPF fix merged

**PR [#1986](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1986)** — "fix(redact): fail closed when OPF is enabled with no categories" — merged 2026-08-14 and shipped in **v0.10.1** (2026-08-18). It's the changelog's Fixed bullet at `CHANGELOG.md:35`:

> The OpenAI privacy filter fails closed when it is enabled with no effective categories, instead of stamping `Entire-OPF-Applied: true` on commits it never scanned — which permanently exempted them from later rewrites

This traces back to Chetan Reddy's **private security report** via Plain (thread T-139, 2026-08-06) — the PR itself was kept neutral with no reporter mention precisely because it was a private report, with release-note credit promised for when it shipped.

## How we've credited contributors in the past

The convention is a `### Thanks` section per release: `Thanks to @handle for <specific thing they did>!` — one line per person (or combined with commas for several small contributions), always naming the concrete contribution rather than a generic thank-you. Two relevant precedents:

- **Reporter-style credit exists**, in this very release: "Thanks to @MuskanPaliwal for *tracking down* the checkpoint metadata bloat…" — so crediting a finder, not just a patch author, is established.
- **@ChetanReddyC has been credited before** as a code contributor: "Thanks to @ChetanReddyC for fixing `entire enable` so it no longer re-enables disabled repos!" — so the handle is consistent with prior credits.

## The credit I added

Appended to v0.10.1's Thanks section (`CHANGELOG.md:56`):

> Thanks to @ChetanReddyC for privately reporting that the OpenAI privacy filter, when enabled with no effective categories, stamped `Entire-OPF-Applied: true` on commits it never scanned — fixed in this release by failing closed at push time!

One deliberate wording choice: the reply sent to Chetan originally promised rejection "at settings validation," but the shipped fix is a **push-time abort** (stronger — settings-load rejection was rejected because hooks swallow Load errors, which would have silently disabled OPF). The credit line says "failing closed at push time" explicitly, which closes out that clarify-in-the-release-note follow-up.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Private security reports get a different credit path here: the fix PR (#1986) stayed reporter-neutral so the vulnerability window wasn't advertised pre-release, and public credit lands only in the changelog once the fix has shipped — a lightweight coordinated-disclosure pattern.
- The fix chose push-time fail-closed over settings-validation rejection because of a failure-mode asymmetry: hooks swallow `settings.Load()` errors, so validation-time rejection would have *silently disabled* OPF — the opposite of fail-closed.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
